result.summary: This PR converts DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan's internal mutex from a RecursiveMutex to a non-recursive Mutex, part of the project-wide effort tracked in issue #19303 to remove recursive locking. It splits public self-locking entry points from internal lock-held helper methods, removes external LOCK(cs_desc_man) call sites in wallet.cpp, rpc code, and fuzz harnesses, and moves address-availability notifications outside the lock so synchronous GUI callbacks can safely re-enter. A final scripted-diff commit renames cs_desc_man to m_desc_mutex to match project naming conventions, and a new regression test covers notification ordering under various operations.
result.problem: Recursive mutexes can mask lock-ordering bugs and make it harder to reason about correctness; the project is systematically removing them (#19303) to reduce the risk of subtle deadlocks or reentrancy bugs in wallet code that maintainers and future contributors would otherwise have to debug.

resolved_concerns: pablomartin4btc questioned whether removing the shared lock around two descriptor reads in listdescriptors could break atomicity; author explained cs_wallet is held across both calls, resolving the concern.
pablomartin4btc suggested a readability improvement in addhdkey(); author implemented it in a follow-up push.

result.card: This PR converts DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan's cs_desc_man from a RecursiveMutex to a plain non-recursive Mutex, part of the project-wide #19303 effort to eliminate recursive locking in Bitcoin Core. It splits public self-locking entry points from lock-held internal helpers, removes external LOCK() call sites across wallet.cpp, RPC code, and fuzz harnesses, and relocates address-availability notifications outside the lock so synchronous callbacks can safely re-enter; a scripted-diff renames the mutex to m_desc_mutex. Two maintainers (pablomartin4btc, hebasto) gave concept ACKs, with pablomartin4btc reviewing commit-by-commit and one atomicity question resolved by the author's explanation that cs_wallet already covers the relevant reads. The PR is clean and mergeable, having just been rebased, with no open objections. It solves no active bug but preventively reduces the risk of subtle lock-ordering issues in wallet descriptor code, making it worthwhile but deferrable within the wallet category.
